title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming & structured response formatting
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer fully in parity with /v1/chat.completions for params, role handling, stop sequences/logprobs, streaming stability, function/tool-calling semantics, and structured response formatting. This PR maps user-facing OpenAI parameters to Redwood internal APIs, fixes streaming edge-cases (partial function-call chunks and role-boundary events), and ensures logprobs/stop behaviour matches OpenAI semantics. Includes docs and compatibility examples.

Summary of changes: unified param parsing (temperature/top_p/n/max_tokens/stop/logprobs), role normalization (system/user/assistant handling + role aliases), streaming event contract updates (stable chunk boundaries, explicit role markers, function_call streaming events), logprobs passthrough for token-level scoring, and response_format support for structured outputs (JSON/schema enforcement + graceful fallback). Also adds integration tests validating parity across common edge-cases (multiple stop tokens, nested function calls, streaming truncation).

Compatibility notes: existing Redwood API remains unchanged for internal clients. The OpenAI-compat path is opt-in behind the openai_compat config flag at runtime. Function/tool calling follows OpenAI semantics: partial tool_call payloads are emitted during streaming and a final tool_call.completed event is sent with aggregated args. Stop/logprobs behavior is gated to requests that set logprobs or stop explicitly; we preserve legacy Redwood fallback when parameters are absent.

Rollout: feature flag rollout with canary in us-west-2 for 48h, followed by global release. Performance: microbenchmarks show <1% median latency regression for standard chat workloads; batching and KV-cache behavior unchanged.
